My parents’ names were Edward and Elizabeth Vaughan. There were six children--Jane, Hugh, Robert, Edward, John and Mary. Edward lives in the old home at the present time. His address is: “Dugoed Bach, Dinas Mowddwy, Mereoneth Sheir, G.

6355-locusts-and-wild-honey.creator: Unknown
6355-locusts-and-wild-honey.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ling-place and be overwhelmed by the steam and the smoke. But bees appear to be more eager for bread in the spring than for honey: their supply of this article, perhaps, does not keep as well as their stores of the latter; hence fresh bread, in the shape of new pollen, is diligently sought for.

8998-paris-as-it-was-and-as-it-is-a-sket.title: Paris As It Was And As It Is A Sketch Of The French Capital
8998-paris-as-it-was-and-as-it-is-a-sket.creator: Unknown
8998-paris-as-it-was-and-as-it-is-a-sket.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. on arriving at Paris after an absence of ten or twelve years--Tumult in the streets considerably diminished since the revolution--No liveries seen--Streets less dangerous than formerly to pedestrians--Visits paid to different persons by the author--Price of lodgings nearly doubled since 1789 --The author takes apartments in a private house.

arxiv-2003-13872.title: Snake Graphs from Triangulated Orbifolds This paper is a contribution to the Special Issue on Cluster Algebras. The full collection is available at https://www.emis.de/journals/SIGMA/cluster-algebras.html
arxiv-2003-13872.creator: Esther BANAIAN and Elizabeth KELLEY
arxiv-2003-13872.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Esther BANAIAN and Elizabeth KELLEY. We give an explicit combinatorial formula for the Laurent expansion of any arc or closed curve on an unpunctured triangulated orbifold. We do this by extending the snake graph construction of Musiker, Schiffler, and Williams to unpunctured orbifolds. In the case of an ordinary arc, this gives a combinatorial proof of positivity to the generalized cluster algebra from this orbifold.

arxiv-2102-00267.title: Inertial Proximal Deep Learning Alternating Minimization for Efficient Neutral Network Training
arxiv-2102-00267.creator: Linbo Qiao, Tao SunHengyue Pan, Dongsheng Li
arxiv-2102-00267.description: Abstract In recent years, the Deep Learning Alternating Minimization (DLAM), which is actually the alternating minimization applied to the penalty form of the deep neutral networks training, has been developed as an alternative algorithm to overcome several drawbacks of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) algorithms.

arxiv-2102-13230.title: RECONSTRUCTING TRIANGULATIONS OF 3 3 -MANIFOLDS FROM THEIR INTERSECTION MATRIX
arxiv-2102-13230.creator: Jorge L. Arocha, Jorge Fernández-Hidalgo
arxiv-2102-13230.description: Abstract The intersection matrix of a simplicial complex has entries equal to the rank of the intersection of its facets. In [ 1 ] the authors prove the intersection matrix is enough to determine a triangulation of a surface up to isomorphism.

arxiv-2104-07817.title: Quantum advantage and noise reduction in distributed quantum computing
arxiv-2104-07817.creator: J. Avron, Ofer Casper, Ilan Rozen
arxiv-2104-07817.description: Abstract Distributed quantum computing can give substantial noise reduction due to shallower circuits. An experiment illustrates the advantages in the case of Grover search. This motivates studying the quantum advantage of the distributed version of the Simon and Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm.

arxiv-2202-03386.title: Closed Ricci Flows with Singularities Modeled on Asymptotically Conical Shrinkers
arxiv-2202-03386.creator: Maxwell Stolarski
arxiv-2202-03386.description: Abstract . Given an asymptotically conical, shrinking, gradient Ricci soliton, we show that there exists a Ricci flow solution on a closed manifold that forms a finite-time singularity modeled on the given soliton. No symmetry or Kähler assumptions on the soliton are required. The proof provides a precise asymptotic description of the singularity formation. 1.

arxiv-2306-12990.title: Slowly Rotating Accretion Flow Around SMBH in Elliptical Galaxy: Case With Outflow
arxiv-2306-12990.creator: Razieh Ranjbar, Shahram Abbassi
arxiv-2306-12990.description: Abstract Observational evidence and many numerical simulations show the existence of wind (i.e., uncollimated outflow) in accretion systems of the elliptical galaxy center. One of the primary aims of this study is to investigate the solutions of slowly rotating accretion flows around the supermassive black hole with outflow.

arxiv-2308-05646.title: AST-MHSA : Code Summarization using Multi-Head Self-Attention
arxiv-2308-05646.creator: Yeshwanth Nagaraj, Ujjwal Gupta
arxiv-2308-05646.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Yeshwanth Nagaraj, Ujjwal Gupta. Code summarization aims to generate concise natural language descriptions for source code. The prevailing approaches adopt transformer-based encoder-decoder architectures, where the Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) of the source code is utilized for encoding structural information. However, ASTs are much longer than the corresponding source code, and existing methods ignore this size constraint by directly feeding the entire linearized AST into the encoders.

arxiv-2309-00820.title: Jupiter Atmospheric Models and Outer Boundary Conditions for Giant Planet Evolutionary Calculations CoolTLusty ( Hubeny & Lanz 1995 ; Sudarsky et al. 2000 ; Sudarsky et al. 2003 ; Sudarsky et al. 2005 ; Burrows et al. 2008 ) . Relevant boundary condition entropy tables used for generating our figure
arxiv-2309-00820.creator: Yi-Xian Chen, Adam Burrows, Ankan Sur, Roberto Tejada Arevalo
arxiv-2309-00820.description: Abstract We present updated atmospheric tables suitable for calculating the post-formation evolution and cooling of Jupiter and Jupiter-like exoplanets. These tables are generated using a 1D radiative transfer modeling code that incorporates the latest opacities and realistic prescriptions for stellar irradiation and ammonia clouds.

arxiv-2402-10267.title: Identification is Pointless: Quantum Coordinates, Localisation of Events, and the Quantum Hole Argument
arxiv-2402-10267.creator: Viktoria Kabel, Anne-Catherine de la Hamette, Luca Apadula, Carlo Cepollaro, Henrique Gomes, Jeremy Butterfield, Časlav Brukner
arxiv-2402-10267.description: Abstract The study of quantum reference frames (QRFs) is motivated by the idea of taking into account the quantum properties of the reference frames used, explicitly or implicitly, in our description of physical systems. Like classical reference frames, QRFs can be used to define physical quantities relationally. Unlike their classical analogue, they relativise the notions of superposition and entanglement.

arxiv-2410-21024.title: Breccia and basalt classification of thin sections of Apollo rocks with deep learning Journal: Acta Astronautica
arxiv-2410-21024.creator: Freja Thoresen, Aidan Cowley, Romeo Haak, Jonas Lewe, Clara Moriceau, Piotr Knapczyk, Victoria S. Engelschiøn
arxiv-2410-21024.description: Abstract Human exploration of the moon is expected to resume in the next decade, following the last such activities in the Apollo programme time. One of the major objectives of returning to the Moon is to continue retrieving geological samples, with a focus on collecting high-quality specimens to maximize scientific return.

arxiv-2412-01301.title: Universal Spreading Dynamics in Quasiperiodic Non-Hermitian Systems
arxiv-2412-01301.creator: Ze-Yu Xing 1, 2, Shu Chen 1, 2, Haiping Hu 1, 2
arxiv-2412-01301.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ze-Yu Xing 1, 2, Shu Chen 1, 2, Haiping Hu 1, 2. Non-Hermitian systems exhibit a distinctive type of wave propagation, due to the intricate interplay of non-Hermiticity and disorder. Here, we investigate the spreading dynamics in the archetypal non-Hermitian Aubry-André model with quasiperiodic disorder.

arxiv-2505-19631.title: Segment First or Comprehend First? Explore the Limit of Unsupervised Word Segmentation with Large Language Models
arxiv-2505-19631.creator: Zihong Zhang, Liqi He, Zuchao Li, Lefei Zhang, Hai Zhao, Bo Du
arxiv-2505-19631.description: Abstract Word segmentation stands as a cornerstone of Natural Language Processing (NLP). Based on the concept of "comprehend first, segment later", we propose a new framework to explore the limit of unsupervised word segmentation with Large Language Models (LLMs) and evaluate the semantic understanding capabilities of LLMs based on word segmentation.

arxiv-2601-04267.title: Information Theoretic Optimal Surveillance for Epidemic Prevalence in Networks
arxiv-2601-04267.creator: Ritwick Mishra, Abhijin Adiga, Madhav Marathe, S. S. Ravi, Ravi Tandon, Anil Vullikanti
arxiv-2601-04267.description: Abstract Estimating the true prevalence of an epidemic outbreak is a key public health problem. This is challenging because surveillance is usually resource intensive and biased. In the network setting, prior work on cost sensitive disease surveillance has focused on choosing a subset of individuals (or nodes) to minimize objectives such as probability of outbreak detection.

catholic-encyclopedia-1913-pope-agapetus.creator: James Loughlin

pmc-10508344.title: Enhancing nursing education to bolster nurse governance: insights from nurse managers
pmc-10508344.creator: Sujin Choi
pmc-10508344.description: AimIn South Korea, the level of nursing governance is moving toward shared governance. This study sought to explore nursing education contents in undergraduate nursing programs necessary to improve the governance of nurses from the perspectives of nurse managers.MethodsThe study employs thematic analysis following the guidelines outlined in the Consolidated Criteria for Reporting Qualitative Research utilizing a qualitative research design.

pmc-10571748.title: Evaluating the Activity of Pigs with Radio-Frequency Identification and Virtual Walking Distances
pmc-10571748.creator: Anita Kapun, Felix Adrion, Eva Gallmann
pmc-10571748.description: Simple SummaryThe greater the number of animals, the harder it becomes to monitor the health status of individual animals. The purpose of this study was to calculate a measure of activity for individual pigs in a fattening barn by using an automatic detection system. The results show changes in the activity data of group-housed pigs during fattening periods.

pmc-11514418.title: Recent efficacy and long-term survival of Astragalus polysaccharide combined with gemcitabine and S-1 in pancreatic cancer
pmc-11514418.creator: Guang-Yu Li, Jing Jiang
pmc-11514418.description: BACKGROUNDPancreatic cancer is a highly malignant tumor with a rapid progression rate and a high susceptibility to infiltration and metastasis. Astragalus polysaccharide (APS), a pure Chinese medicine preparation primarily made from the traditional Chinese herb Astragalus, plays a positive role in the treatment of many malignant tumors.

pmc-11547696.title: Health Benefits Beyond the Scale: The Role of Diet and Nutrition During Weight Loss Programmes
pmc-11547696.creator: Francisca Contreras, Werd Al-Najim, Carel W. le Roux
pmc-11547696.description: Introduction: Obesity management strategies such as caloric restriction, very-low-calorie diets (VLCDs), and meal replacements can lead to moderate short-term weight loss. However, many patients face significant challenges in maintaining these results. Personalized interventions, including behavioral counseling and physical activity, have been shown to improve long-term adherence and success.

pmc-11600209.title: Overcoming Biopotency Barriers: Advanced Oral Delivery Strategies for Enhancing the Efficacy of Bioactive Food Ingredients
pmc-11600209.creator: Ling Liu, David Julian McClements, Xuebo Liu, Fuguo Liu
pmc-11600209.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Bioactive food ingredients contribute to the promotion and maintenance of human health and wellbeing. However, these functional ingredients often exhibit low biopotency after food processing or gastrointestinal transit. Well‐designed oral delivery systems can increase the ability of bioactive food ingredients to resist harsh environments inside and outside the human body, as well as allow for controlled or triggered release of bioactives to specific sites in the gastrointestinal tract or other tissues and organs.

pmc-11675241.title: Serial Examination of Platelet Function Tests Might Predict Prognosis of Patients with Acute Ischemic Stroke—A Cohort Study
pmc-11675241.creator: Hsin-Ju Ho, Li-Ching Wu, Yu-Wei Chen, Sonu M M Bhaskar
pmc-11675241.description: Background: This study investigated whether point-of-care platelet function measurements could predict favorable outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Antiplatelet agents, such as aspirin, are known to reduce the risk of recurrent stroke by 20–30%. However, identifying nonresponders to therapy remains a clinical challenge.

pmc-11709982.title: Cognitive Profile Subgroups Among Non‐demented Older Adults and their Associations with AD Neuroimaging Measures
pmc-11709982.creator: Alice M Hahn, Heather E Volk, Marilyn S Albert, Anja Soldan, The BIOCARD Research Team
pmc-11709982.description: BackgroundAlthough it is well established that lower cognitive performance, on average, is associated with a greater risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease (AD) dementia, it is unclear whether distinct cognitively‐defined subgroups exist among non‐demented older adults and whether such profiles map onto distinct AD neuroimaging measure profiles.

pmc-12510563.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal post-translational modifications in osteosarcoma progression and tumor microenvironment
pmc-12510563.creator: Yue Cui, Yue Wu, Dongyu Jiang, Tao Ding, Yisheng Chen, Zu Ye, Zu Ye, Zu Ye
pmc-12510563.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Emerging evidence suggests that post-translational modifications (PTMs) contribute to osteosarcoma pathogenesis, yet their exact molecular roles require further elucidation. Using the AddModuleScore method, we classified tumor cells on the basis of PTMs scores via single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq). The robust cell type decomposition (RCTD) approach was then applied to map these single-cell groupings onto spatial transcriptomics (ST), enabling the analysis of cell dependencies and the identification of distinct tumor cell subtypes.

pmc-12756145.title: High-resolution single-cell RNA sequencing using canFam4 reveals novel immune subsets and checkpoint programs in healthy dogs
pmc-12756145.creator: Myung-Chul Kim, Taeeun Gu, Hyeewon Seo, Yewon Moon, Nicholas Borcherding, Ryan Kolb, Yubin Kim, Youngmin Yun, Woo-Jin Song, Chung-Young Lee, Hyun Je Kim, Weizhou Zhang
pmc-12756145.description: IntroductionSingle-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution profiling of immune heterogeneity. Although previous studies have mapped the single-cell transcriptomic atlases of peripheral leukocytes in healthy dogs, the identification and functional characterization of distinct immune subsets remain incomplete.MethodsWe constructed a single-cell atlas of peripheral leukocytes from six healthy small-breed dogs using the 10x Genomics platform and the updated canFam4 genome.

pmc-13156623.title: Re: Grzegorz L. Fojecki, Elena Atrakhimovich, Martin Bruhn, et al. Reduced Rate of Complications with Transperineal Prostate Biopsy: Real-world Data from a National Cohort Derived from the Danish Prostate Cancer Registry. Eur Urol Open Sci 2026;87:1–7
pmc-13156623.creator: Xiaowei Zhang, Zheng Wang
pmc-13156623.description: d magnitude of the observed association are impressive: as TP biopsy uptake rose rapidly, the estimated 7-d hospitalization risk remained at around 0.8% for TP versus at approximately 4.8% for TR, even after adjustment. This is an important real-world contribution to the current discussion on biopsy safety.

pmc-13194687.title: Population genetic diversity in the annual breeding area of the Spodoptera frugiperda in China
pmc-13194687.creator: J R Lin, J Zhang, Y Zou, Z W Wu
pmc-13194687.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The fall armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda), a globally invasive pest, has established persistent populations in China since its invasion in late 2018, posing a continuous threat to agriculture due to its potential for rapid adaptation and insecticide resistance evolution.

pmc-13352746.title: Perceived vs. actual cigarette and waterpipe dependence in Lebanon: a cross-sectional study of social desirability across demographic subgroups
pmc-13352746.creator: David Karam, Chadia Haddad, Hala Sacre, Rana Hatem, Fouad Sakr, Sandrella Bou Malhab, Clara Gerges, Dalal Youssef, Roy Eid, Georgia Chkayban, Aline Hajj, Marguerite Ghostin, Pascale Salameh
pmc-13352746.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTobacco use is a significant global public health issue, increasingly affecting low- and middle-income countries. In culturally sensitive contexts like Lebanon, self-reported smoking may be unreliable, particularly among socially restricted groups such as women and youth.

pmc-13672699.title: Perspectives and experiences of nurse academics teaching reflective practice to undergraduate Bachelor of Nursing students: a scoping review
pmc-13672699.creator: Lisa Speedie, Gulzar Malik, Jacqueline Johnston, Christine East
pmc-13672699.description: Background:Reflective practice is essential in nursing education, as it promotes critical thinking and fosters professional growth. Although it is acknowledged in higher education and included in university attributes, the perspectives and experiences of nurse academics who teach it remain underexplored.

pmc-13679867.title: Psychosocial Distress and Radiation Treatment Interruptions in Patients With Cancer Using Machine Learning and Regression: Retrospective Cohort Study
pmc-13679867.creator: Soheil Hashtarkhani, Christopher L Brett, Fekede Asefa Kumsa, Rezaur Rashid, Parnian Kheirkhah Rahimabad, Saba Kheirinejad, Robert L Davis, David L Schwartz, Arash Shaban-Nejad
pmc-13679867.description: BackgroundUninterrupted delivery of radiation therapy is critical to cancer treatment quality. Unplanned radiation treatment interruptions compromise tumor control and survival. Although previous studies have explored clinical and sociodemographic factors influencing treatment adherence, the role of psychosocial distress and related symptoms remains unclear.
